questions.question: The ability of an ecosystem to recover from disturbances is known as: a). Resilience b). Resistance c). Adaptation d). Stability
questions.solution_html:
• The study of antibiotic resistance illustrates the principle of evolution by showing
  • how bacteria adapt to survive when exposed to antibiotics. When antibiotics are used
  • bacteria with random genetic mutations that make them resistant can survive and
  • reproduce, while others die. Over time, the population shifts to mostly resistant
  • bacteria, demonstrating natural selection—only the fittest survive and pass on their
  • genes. This real-time evolution is a clear example of how selective pressure (like
  • antibiotic use) leads to changes in populations, just as Charles Darwin described in his
  • theory of evolution. (U, CO6)
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: theory of evolution. (U, CO6)

  • nowhere else and have lost a significant portion of their natural habitat. Their

  • biodiversity, provide essential ecosystem services like climate regulation, pollination
  • and water purification, and help maintain ecological balance. Protecting these
  • hotspots also safeguards the livelihoods of people who depend on these
  • ecosystems.(U,CO3)
